AT LEAST FOUR VINTAGES OF THIS ANALYSIS EXIST, and section 4 draws from several. In order: a 17-session fit (711/711 files, 293,760 rows, signed means -0.53/-0.37/-0.22/-0.06/+0.13 dB), described by CONTEXT.md section 9 and recorded by docs_audit_20260802 as already superseded and absent from artifacts; the 2026-07-29 23-session refit (420,480 rows, 909/18) that section 4's census line and its C31o theta -1.578 per-animal figure come from, receipt overwritten; a 2026-08-02 refit that section 4's A_corpus q-values come from, surviving only as a draft annotation; `glmm_pre_fullcorpus_20260805` (23 sessions, 84,096 obs) that section 4's V3a/d estimates and q-values come from, still on disk; and the current 2026-08-12 22-session run. Writing successive runs into the same directory name is what destroyed the first two. Any correction must preserve the current artifact rather than repeating that pattern.

RECEIPT SCRIPT POINTERS GO STALE TOO, not only data paths. The current receipt.json names script `compute_channel_band_power_census_v2.py`; no such file exists. The script on disk is `omission/scripts/compute_channel_band_power_census.py`, with no `_v2` suffix (verified directly). So a receipt can fail to resolve on BOTH its data path and its script pointer, and neither failure raises an error at read time. This generalizes beyond Fig05: every pre-2026-08-24 receipt in the project cites paths predating the outputs reorganization and the D: -> C:/E: migration.

CENSUS LINE FULLY TRACED 2026-09-02, superseding both verifiers' partial accounts. Verifier 1 called the line untraceable and guessed a transcription from the stimulus census; verifier 2 corrected that to 'a 2026-07-29 run whose receipt was overwritten'. Both were incomplete. Section 4's census line is a COMPOSITE of two surviving artifacts, neither of which is the omission band census: '909 omission-condition files processed, 18 skipped' matches `outputs/lfp_dynamics/omission_tfr_maps_w1500/receipt.json` (2026-07-29, n_files_processed 909, n_files_skipped 18, source_dir D:/workspace/data/tfr_arrays) exactly; '1,236 TFR files scanned, 420,480 rows, 23 sessions' matches `outputs/lfp_dynamics/lfp_band_census_stim/receipt.json`, the STIMULUS-window census. Both files exist today. So the numbers were never lost -- they were composed from two different analyses into one paragraph describing a third.

RESTATEMENT OF THE DEFECT. This is not primarily a staleness problem and not a fabrication problem. No number in section 4 was invented and most remain findable. The defect is COMPOSITION: quantities from different analyses, corpora and dates were assembled under one path and one heading, producing a section that read as a coherent current census although no single run ever produced it. Staleness detection (does the path resolve, is the file newer) would not have caught this; only re-deriving each quoted quantity against a named receipt does.
